coverage_limits: Only the supplied allowed record and the 14 supplied law units are judged; no external search, project history, other case version, or withheld historical final outcome is used.

The supplied segments establish an allegation that respondent no.1 illegally sublet to respondent no.2 and contain a quoted ARC finding that respondent no.1 was the tenant and respondent no.2's claimed tenancy was not proved, but those ARC statements remain lower-court quoted material within the supervisory proceeding and are not silently converted into an independent High Court finding.

The record does not directly establish the factual character of respondent no.2's possession, including whether respondent no.1 surrendered exclusive possession, retained legal possession or control, or otherwise parted with possession within section 14(1)(b).
The supplied record does not establish whether the landlord gave written consent to any subletting, assignment, transfer, or possession arrangement involving respondent no.2.

Payment or alleged payment of rent from respondent no.2's account is preserved as supplied evidence and argument; source location alone does not establish that respondent no.2 became tenant or that a subletting occurred.

The supplied share counts—1250 shares for respondent no.1, 23000 for her son, and 400 for her daughter-in-law—are retained without inferring corporate control, alter-ego status, possession, or absence of subletting.

No court-sanctioned amalgamation, company dissolution, statutory acquisition, banking-company reconstruction, RBI scheme, or bank-transfer scheme involving respondent no.1 and respondent no.2 is supplied; the corporate-amalgamation and banking units therefore cannot supply missing case facts.

The current Delhi statutory reproductions have historical-version status unverified. They are used only for the displayed provisions and are not treated as authenticated historical consolidations for the alleged 1988 arrangement.
The Banking Regulation Act materials are later consolidations containing later amendments and are not used retrospectively to reconstruct rules applicable to the alleged 1988 arrangement.

Hindustan Petroleum is dated September 1988, after the supplied claim that respondent no.2 was tenant from May 1988; its Bombay statutory-acquisition analysis is not used retrospectively or generalized to this Delhi case.

The 1993 New Bank of India scheme post-dates the alleged 1988 arrangement and is specific to New Bank of India and Punjab National Bank; it supplies no retrospective or automatic rule for this tenancy.

The General Radio passage describing Parasaram is a reported-precedent paragraph supplied within another judgment, not an independently supplied full Parasaram opinion; only the proposition actually reproduced in the supplied paragraph is evaluated.

Telesound contains a prima facie discussion in an amalgamation context and expressly reserves the ultimate section 14(1)(b) eviction issue; it is not treated as having resolved that reserved question.
